newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel CPI-linked bond prices up on inflation fea.
newsitem.headline: Israel CPI-linked bond prices up on inflation fea.

text.p: Prices of Israeli CPI-linked bonds continued rising on Thursday on fears of accelerating inflation and amid a tightening supply of inflation-linked bonds, traders said.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct to 107.86
Volume including Makams was an average 151 million shekels.

"CPI-linked bonds rose today on fears of high inflation and on a tightening supply of inflation-linked bonds. The main rises were in the floating-interest CPI-linked bonds, which rose by 0.3 to 0.5 percent," said a trader.
Yields on CPI-linked short bonds were around 4.1-4.2 percent while yields on long bonds were 3.95 percent, the trader said.

The June CPI, published on Tuesday after the close of trading, rose by an unexpectedly high 1.1 percent against a rise of 0.5 percent in May. The rise was due mainly to housing prices and many analysts are predicting a high index in July as well.
"We expect yields on CPI-linked long bonds to continue lower because of the tight supply of bonds," said an investment manager at Jerusalem Capital Markets.

"Unlinked bonds traded steady today, after falling yesterday on the high CPI," the trader said. "Now their yields are stable at 13 to 13.5 percent. At these levels there are buyers because some traders don't really believe inflation is on its way up again."
He said he didn't expect the central bank to raise interest rates at the end of this month but a high July CPI could prompt a rate hike at the end of August.
The Bank of Israel slashed its base lending rate in mid-June by 1.2 percentage points to an annualised 12.7 percent.
Dollar-linked bonds traded steady with a negative trend, traders said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
- Shoshanna Solomon, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
